column1: # seams.tsv (harbor#1425) — one row per contract that crosses a repo boundary: who produces it, who consumes it, where the copy sits, what pins it.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The vendored naming package sat 11 commits behind its producer with 6 of 14 registry files different, and
# nothing compared a copy with its upstream; fleet's schema was "derived from real emitted output" by its consumer; harbor shipped
# no schema at all. A seam is a row, so a copy with no row is red (standard.seam-registered), a row whose copy is gone is red, the
# producer's schema is a path that must exist, and one freshness check reads this file instead of one hard-coded contract.
# standard_version: 2.0.0
# COLUMNS  id <TAB> kind <TAB> producer <TAB> consumer <TAB> copy_path <TAB> pin <TAB> schema <TAB> freshness <TAB> owner <TAB> allowed_lag <TAB> reason
#   id          kebab, unique; what a finding names
#   kind        vendor (a file tree copied byte for byte) | contract (a schema or doc one side owns, the other keeps a copy of)
#               | format (a record shape read in place, no copy) | upstream (a third party's code held here)
#   producer    the system that owns the contract and its schema: harbor, yard, fleet or an outside name
#   consumer    the system that holds the copy or reads the output: harbor, yard, fleet or scaffolded (repos yard creates)
#   copy_path   the consumer's path to the copy (a trailing / is a tree); - when the consumer reads the producer in place
#   pin         where the copy records what it was taken from, <path under copy_path>#<key>, or <path>#<key> from the consumer root;
#               - when nothing records it
#   schema      the producer's path to the schema its own CI validates its output against; - when none exists yet (the row says why)
#   freshness   the control that compares the copy with its producer (check.seam-fresh), or - when there is no copy to compare
#   owner       the family that answers for the seam (terms.tsv, class family)
#   allowed_lag commits touching the producer's files that the pin may trail before a stale copy is a finding; 0 = none
#   reason      why a row carries a lag, a missing schema or no freshness check; - when it needs none
